500th Birthday of Don Isaac Abravanel.

[Chorzów(?) — Mizrachi; culture.] In the premises of the "Mizrachi" in Chorzów[?] a festive academy was held in connection with the 500th birthday of R' Don Isaac Abravanel. Lectures were given by Rabbi Dr. Kalberg on the topic "The last link in the golden chain of Jewish Diaspora history" and by Prof. Kokos[?] on the topic "Abravanel's relation to free philosophy"; both lectures made a strong impression on the audience. S. B.
Eretz Israel Academy in Nowa Wieś.

[Nowa Wieś — Zionism.] In the community hall in Nowa Wieś an imposing Eretz Israel academy was held with the participation of the community president Mr. Sitanger and of the Chorzów[?] rabbi Shapira, and Prof. Kokos[?]. Before a packed hall president Sitanger opened the academy; then H.B.[?] Shifer and Prof. Kokos spoke about Eretz Israel, and the speeches were received with stormy applause.
On the spot a considerable sum of money was collected for the Keren [Kayemet?] LeIsrael.
Great Impression Made by the Visit of the Gaon Rabbi Yitzchak Grossman to Będzin

The few days that Rabbi Grossman, candidate for the rabbinical seat of Będzin, spent in Będzin were turned into festive days. Almost all strata of the Jewish population came to visit the distinguished guest, and everyone could soon convince himself that before him stood a personality of broad and great scope, a rabbi and a gaon in the full sense of the word. It was simply a spiritual pleasure to spend time with him and hear his deep halakhic discussions, which he surely inherited from his great teacher, the Chofetz Chaim, of blessed memory.
Great was the impression of his brilliant sermons, which he delivered in the beit midrash and in the synagogue before the Torah reading, where the synagogue was overflowing with Jews[?], scholars and householders.
The climax was undoubtedly his great and powerful sermon on Shabbat afternoon in the town synagogue, where even the women's gallery was given over to men and was overflowing with people of various tendencies, on whom the rabbi, with his powerful and brilliant sermon, left an unforgettable impression.
Very impressive too was the "Oneg Shabbat" in the "Mizrachi" premises.
—
On Sunday and Monday the rabbi prayed in the Sochaczew [Hasidim's] "shtibl", where he held discussions with a number of the local scholars.
On Tuesday evening the rabbi gave a lecture in the hall of the "Beit Yetomim" (orphanage), to which the town's notables and the Jewish intelligentsia were also invited. On the presidium sat: Ch. Szajn, Yaakov Gutman, Fürstenberg, Trapojer[?] and others.
Mr. L. Guchzajch[?] welcomed the distinguished guest and gave the floor to the rabbi for his lecture on the Jewish situation in the whole world and his hope of "and the children shall return to their own border" (Jer. 31:17).

Campaign for the Hebrew University in Zagłębie and Silesia

As is known, together with the rector of the Hebrew University in Jerusalem, Prof. Bergmann, Messrs. Dr. Berger and Yaakov Magid came to Poland in order to carry out the one-time fund-raising for the University.
The University's budget, already a reduced one, amounts to over 80 thousand pounds. It must partly also be covered by Polish Jewry, if only because over 60 per cent of the students come from Poland.
On Wednesday Messrs. Dr. Berger, Magid and the general secretary of the Society of "Friends of the Hebrew University in Jerusalem", Mr. Poznański, came to Zagłębie.
Under the chairmanship of President Fürstenberg a reception for the above-mentioned guests took place in the gymnasium, arranged by the Będzin branch of the Society of "Friends of the Hebrew University in Jerusalem".
President Fürstenberg welcomed the above-mentioned guests as well as the numerous assembled from Będzin, Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa, Katowice[?] and Strzemieszyce. Dr. Berger then delivered a most interesting lecture on the achievements and the significance of the institution of higher learning on Mount Scopus. The lecturer, who was showered with tumultuous applause, then answered the many questions put to him. A fine lecture was also given by Mr. Magid, in Hebrew and Yiddish.
President Fürstenberg then appealed to the well-to-do and intellectual circles to give proper support to the University, which, after 12 years of its existence, is turning to us for help for the first time.
Dr. Weinzieher thanked President Fürstenberg in the name of all those assembled for his untiring work for the University and assured him that those assembled would do everything to help the institution of higher learning.
— In Sosnowiec, on the initiative of Messrs. Dr. Melaristo[?] and President Sapner[?], a meeting took place which elected a special committee to carry out the campaign. The committee consists of Messrs. President Sapner[?], Dr. Proks[?], Henryk Wigner[?], Dr. Landau and Dr. Lewenhof[?].
Campaign for the Yiddish Secular School System in Zagłębie

These days the annual financial aid campaign for the Yiddish secular schools in the country has begun in Zagłębie.
For this purpose the long-standing, untiring school and cultural activist Mr. M. Mandelman, who has been conducting the school campaigns in Poland for a number of years already, has been specially delegated here by the "TSYSHO" (Central Yiddish School Organization).
On this occasion it is worth recording some important cultural achievements of the "TSYSHO" in recent times.
In honour of the hundredth birthday of Mendele Moykher-Sforim a Mendele exhibition of children's work in the schools of Warsaw and Białystok was arranged.
Thanks to the initiative of the "TSYSHO", a special pavilion devoted to Yiddish secular culture is being organized at the International Paris Exhibition.
For the new school year 1937/38 a pedagogical lyceum will be opened at the Yiddish gymnasium (with state rights) in Vilna. It will take the place of the famous Yiddish Vilna teachers' seminary.
This year's school campaign therefore calls for special attention and must be supported by all circles.

Budget Questions of the Będzin City Council

[Będzin — city council, budget, schools.] (A reply to Mr. Zylberberg).
In the pre-Passover issue of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung", councillor Mr. Ch. Zylberberg, in his article on the budget questions of the Będzin city council, added at the end that the Jewish Left had voted against the subsidy for the Jewish schools. Since[?] this does not agree with reality, I wish to clear up here the inaccuracy in Mr. Zylberberg's article.
Surely nobody will[?] comprehend how it is possible that Jewish left-wing councillors should vote against subsidies for Jewish schools? My comrades and friends overseas, too, who know that I am a councillor and belong to the "Jewish Left", will be quite unable to understand what has happened there to "our" councillor — has he really gone so far that he votes against Jewish schools?
And here[?] I really want to ask Mr. Zylberberg: against which Jewish schools did the Jewish Left vote? Perhaps against the Jewish people's (folk) schools, which unfortunately do not exist in Będzin?
Would that we had Jewish schools here, whether of "Szul-Kult", or at least of CISzO or "Tarbut" — although I am no adherent of the last two types of school — you would have seen, Mr. Zylberberg, how I would have demanded and striven for those schools to be subsidised. I am sure that even the Polish workers' councillors would have taken an interest. But for which Jewish schools were subsidies demanded here?
Had you, Mr. Zylberberg, been objective in this matter, you would have told the truth: that the Magistrate [municipal executive] proposed an item of 1.500 zł. as a subsidy for "private people's schools", but since no such schools — neither Jewish nor Polish — exist in Będzin, the money would have benefited the cheder of the "Agudah" [Agudat Israel] and some little bit the cheder-school of "Mizrachi". But that is not the whole reason why we voted against the item.
It is interesting how the item of 1,500 zł. came to a vote.
In recent years the budget has contained an item of 600 zł. as a subsidy for "private people's schools", of which "Mizrachi" received 125 zł., and the "Agudah" cheder perhaps somewhat more — exactly how much I do not know.
In the present term the Agudah councillors try, as everywhere, to curry favour and flatter — and in general, what is their whole task in the city council anyway? Do they care in the least for the Jewish street[?]? They care only[?] for their Agudah purposes, just as in the kehillas, where they care only for their rabbis, shochtim, etc. But in the city council one cannot obtain subsidies for the latter, and what will they bring to the "Agudah"? So they wanted to make use of the subsidy. Woe[?] to such subsidies of a few hundred zł. against the several hundred thousand zł. that Będzin pays — and in what way would they have obtained it [misprinted "ba-bkumen"]? And this sum "for the Jewish schools" was meant to be the compensation for the cheder[?].
And the Agudah councillors were so happy with this that they had already given up on everything else. The latter happened in the budget committee: there the Jewish representative, who belongs to the "Agudah", did not defend a single Jewish item, but even wanted to reduce the subsidies for Jewish purposes. The same was clearly demonstrated at that same session of the city council, where a "left-wing" councillor, not a Jewish one, a member of the same budget committee, exposed the hypocrisy of the Agudah councillors, who care only for themselves. And to the reproach of the left-wing councillors, that same Agudah[?] representative defended himself[?] before the whole plenum aloud with the excuse that he had overlooked[?] the Jewish items! Quite a find!
And in return for the good that the Agudah does us, for all the troubles they cause — they were to be given the pleasure of rejoicing over the item of 1500 zł.; and on top of that, for whom? For those lads who are ready to tear the eyes out of every Jew who does not travel to Ger [Góra Kalwaria, i.e. is not a Gerrer Hasid]?
On the other hand, we workers' councillors did not want to give up the former item of 600 zł. Let at least the Mizrachi school have it, although we are also very far from the latter. However, I explained to my comrades of the Workers' Club that Mizrachi is a national-religious school and that the financial side of the school does not depend on the Mizrachi leadership, but the whole institution is a cooperative of the teachers and technical[?] staff; and we voted for the item only on condition that the sum be paid to Mizrachi.
The item passed, which made Mr. Zylberberg, as a Mizrachi councillor, very pleased, because the Agudah councillors walked out over it in a huff, and as people said at the time, Mr. Zylberberg "pulled it off the Turkish way!" And now you play the innocent, and in return for our kindness you want to run us down. But in future I ask you not to worry about us; better tell the public how things look among you bourgeois councillors — that you cannot come to an agreement among yourselves, and that for almost 2 years now you have been in the city council and still cannot form your "club" [caucus]! And above all, tell about those few of your representatives who vote against the interests of their own voters.
Aron Hampel.
“Maccabi” and Physical Education.

[Sosnowiec — sport and physical education; article.]
The “Maccabi” in Sosnowiec — the chronicle tells us — has proclaimed a month of propaganda and of recruiting new members.
Sosnowiec society ought to take an interest in this, the only Jewish sports institution in our town, and to demonstrate [?] its understanding for physical education by joining the ranks of the gymnasts.
The “Maccabi” is an ideological [?] organisation, but one whose Zionist, non-factional stance is, so to speak, its only creed, and whose aim is [?] to revive the Jewish people through the physical and moral education of the youth in the spirit of national discipline.
Through the physical training of the youth the “Maccabi” creates a healthy national element and vigorous pioneers of revival.
This task is an important one, because the youth is the material of the people, on which its strength and vitality depend. How often do we unconsciously repeat the old formula “a sound mind in a sound body”; we recommend it to others, yet do not apply it to ourselves. We forget the duty to care for our own organism and health.
Only systematic work in physical education can give energy, liveliness, zest for life, alertness and sharpness of mind. A young organism grows, develops and gathers energy that seeks [?] an outlet, and it can find one only in methodical, soundly conducted work in physical education in the sports clubs.
Usually we make sport a “forbidden fruit”; the youth is not given its proper place at the proper time. We do not go along with the healthy demands of the youth, and we have no understanding for the living needs of the youth, at a time when we ought to guide and lead them and not hold them back.
We must set physical education on its proper pedestal and make of it a regular and programmatic occupation for boys and girls.
Youth in general is drawn to sports exercises. Everyone is attracted by the prospect of a healthy and straight body, of health [?] and sporting distinction. But not often does it find this in clubs where the work in physical education would be conducted methodically, according to a programme and under proper conditions. Therefore everyone should join the “Maccabi”, which has all these conditions and can ensure everyone a proper physical training.
L. Rozensztajn.
Pan Władek Has Bought a "Shekel"...

[Sosnowiec — satirical feuilleton; the Zionist shekel campaign.]
As a rule I have nothing whatever in common with Pan Władek for a whole year round. He is a Jew who is occupied day and night with the "laws of poker"; for several years now he has been learning to play "bridge" and simply cannot grasp the art. Twice a day he sips black coffee at the "Rex" [café], and twice a year (Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur) you will find him in the "German" synagogue. He has a pair of moustaches — they are as long as the Jewish exile. All his strength he puts into the moustaches, and as if out of spite they keep falling into his mouth and will not let him trim them "upright". Against Jews he is — no evil eye — "to destroy and to kill"; he is especially incensed at the Zionists, with their congresses, campaigns and Palestine, and he never speaks of Zionists otherwise than as "scoundrels" (szubrawcy) and "thieves" (złodzieje) [?]. If he hears a Yiddish word, it throws him completely; then his moustaches grow even longer, and in his great agitation one hears nothing more from him than "cursed jargon" (przeklęty żargon) and "disgusting Jews" (wstrętni Żydzi) [?].
Year after year, when the shekel campaign used to be proclaimed, I would set off on a visit to Pan Władek and start "persuading" him. But all my effort was a blessing in vain. From year to year his hatred of Zionism grew, and his collection of curses and insults became enormously enriched. Thus I went to him 16 years in a row with the [?] shekel, and Pan Władek formally showed me where the door is.
But I did not want to break my tradition, and this year too I set off to him for a portion of bitter curses. I came to Pan Władek one afternoon, just as he was catching a nap on his "modern couch" (nowoczesny tapczan), with his moustaches clamped in a pair of nickel clips. He jumped up at once, however, and invited me into his study, where he always used to settle his "formal matters" (formalne sprawy). His joy at seeing me was so great that I thought Pan Władek had gone out of his mind. He tried to put his moustaches in order and smiled at me good-naturedly without stopping. He did not let me get a word in at all; he talked as if through fire and water [?] and "praised" the Zionists endlessly. Suddenly he pulled out of his pocket a gilden and 20 groszy and asked me to give him a shekel.
I looked at Pan Władek as at a madman [printed "meshugoim"] and slowly began writing out a shekel for him.
"Panie Luks," Pan Władek meanwhile began to talk politics, "but [all the Jews?] (ale … [?]) — how can your Palestine take them in like that? Why, it's a terribly tiny country! (to przecież strasznie malutki kraj!)"
"Don't be afraid, sir (niech się pan nie boi)," I went on [?] [unclear word] to Pan Władek, "all as one, with you, Panie Władku, at the head, Palestine will be able to take in. If little Jews begin by the millions to gather in the Land of Israel, we shall build houses in the air, on the sea, on the Jordan, and one by one [?] we shall begin to move on up across Transjordan, a little bit over Syria and [?]... all right (już dobrze)..."
"Just so (a tak właśnie)," Pan Władek began tugging at his left moustache, "and how is it with this Transjordan, because I want to vote with this shekel for Transjordan! (jak tam z tym Ewer ha-Jarden, bo ja chcę głosować z tym szeklem na Ewer ha-Jarden!)..."
"'With this Transjordan' is excellent," I handed Pan Władek the shekel. "Firstly, the Arabs are fleeing from there en masse to Palestine, to our little Jews, and secondly, terrible epidemics of typhus and malaria have lately broken out there, which ship [?] whole camps of Arabs off to the next world. When Transjordan has been emptied of Arabs, our little Jews will swim across the Jordan in a jiffy — and there they will make prosperity (i tam zrobią prosperity)."
"As I love God (jak Boga kocham)," Pan Władek rubbed his two coarse hands for joy, "[?] I am setting off to Palestine (wybieram się do Palestyny)... but.., but... if you, gentlemen (panowie), could overcome the terrible heat there in your Palestine, it would be salvation for the whole population (zbawienie dla całej ludności)... When I remember the terrible heat of Eretz Israel, I am seized by horror (zgroza) [?], a mortal fear of the whole country."
"A trifle (drobnostka)," I began to calm Pan Władek. "Firstly, here in Poland the heat is no less than in Palestine, and you must [printed "you have courage"] first travel to Gdynia in order to enjoy the sea, and afterwards the 'Orędownik' [nationalist anti-Jewish daily, Poznań] gets to write that 'the Jews are polluting Gdynia, [?] and in general the whole sea'. But there, in Palestine, at every step you have a broad and beautiful sea, which you can even parcel out into plots and bathe [?] (i kąpać się …); besides, we do have a few clever Jewish heads with all sorts of 'inventions' (wynalazki). There will surely be found such scholars as Hitler drove out of Germany, and they will surely devise some remedy against the heat, just as they have thought up remedies against locusts, against malaria and other plagues."
"Oh, how clever you are, sir (o, jaki pan mądry)," Pan Władek clapped me on the shoulders and treated me to a cigar. "Tell me then [?], Panie Luks, what is going on there in that Palestine with the socialists? Your [?] 'Nasz Przegląd' [Polish-language Jewish daily, Warsaw] does not stop for a [single?] minute writing about the leftists, who are even worse than the Bolsheviks and want to divide up the orange groves of the capitalists and colonists. I am terribly afraid of socialists (ja się socjalistów strasznie boję)," and Pan Władek began fanning his face with a newspaper because of the heat that had suddenly come over him.
"Nothing to fear! (nie ma strachu!)" I laughed out loud at Pan Władek's helplessness. "They are indeed socialists with red flags, and they sing the 'Internationale' on the First of May, but there is nobody to be afraid of. Only, if you are nevertheless afraid of the 'red people' in Eretz Israel, then take me along on your '[?]' to Eretz Israel. I'll show you, and you'll see that no one will even touch your moustaches, and they will hang down there with the same aristocratic charm right to your very mouth, as here at home in Sosnowiec."
Pan Władek burst into ringing laughter for great joy. He carefully put away the 'shekel', hid it in his pocket and bade me a hearty farewell. On my way out he asked me to come and fetch him on the day of the 'voting' (głosowanie), because for the first time he does not dare go alone to a Zionist 'vote'. "But, but," he shouted after me, "I will vote for Transjordan, for all the seas [?], so that there be no heat waves in your Palestine and so that there be no socialists! (żeby nie było upałów w waszej Palestynie i żeby nie było socjalistów)..."
Luks.
On Creating a Central Cultural Society for Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — culture; article.]
P. Blumenkrantz (Sosnowiec)
Before presenting the main project — a few remarks that bear on the matter itself.
We must admit, after all, that despite the months of propaganda and the successful exhibitions of the pitiful few Jewish people's schools, our cultural life is going down and down. Cultural work in the small towns is a zero; activity in the larger towns is undergoing a permanent decline. Every so often other societies are founded, chairmen are elected, but nothing concrete gets done. All these attempts do not live long and die as soon as the rent has to be paid.
It goes without saying that the main reason is [printed "in", probably for "is"] the desperate Jewish economic situation; it really is impossible to demand of a starving, dejected Jew or an unemployed young man that he think about the spirit.
But besides the main reason there is yet another, better-known [?] reason that has caused the present state of culture in the larger Jewish settlements: the disease is called decentralisation.
More clearly:
That two Jews have three opinions is known to everyone; that where ten Jews live, five organisations are founded — is also well known.
But besides pure party work, every party also has the ambition to conduct cultural activity. The upshot of it all is that every party, or even an economic organisation, has a library, a stage director, a conductor — and in the end nothing is done except worrying how to squeeze [?] out of the members another quarter's rent.
Cultural work in all the larger Jewish settlements has the same fate as Sholem Aleichem's orphan: everyone wipes his nose until it becomes red and swollen. For one must remember that besides the cultural work at "Poalei Zion", the "Bund", Agudah, Mizrachi, Torah ve-Avodah, Zionists, Grossmanists [followers of Meir Grossman], Revisionists, religious artisans, Halutz, General Zionists, "Hehalutz O.H." [?] (not counting the small traders, artisans etc.), every town also has pure cultural organisations that have to look after singing, music, local studies, Judaistics and what not!
And precisely because of the great abundance of caretakers the Yiddish word has become homeless ["farvoglt"], the Yiddish book forgotten and Yiddish cultural work put to shame!
One thing the cultural activists and individuals do not want to remember (we [printed "mer"] are speaking of the larger provincial towns): that if Warsaw can afford a decentralisation of cultural work, because it concentrates a large number of capable [?] cultural forces, the provincial towns cannot afford it.
No provincial town may create a separate "kloyzl" [little prayer-house, i.e. club] for hiking, a separate one for singing and a separate one for reading a Yiddish book.
In a big city a merchant can allow himself to open a shop of neckties only, and he does well. In a small town he must keep in his store kindling wood, kerosene, glassware, shoelaces ["shnuravadles", Polish sznurowadła], earrings and purses [?]. Lost — if not, he must pack up the shop.
• • •
The whole introduction was meant to show that we mean nothing malicious by our project.
We also want to note that if in all the larger provincial towns [the situation] is highly unsatisfactory, the situation in Zagłębie is even worse.
Będzin stands better in this respect; on the other hand the situation in Sosnowiec and Dąbrowa is simply disgraceful.
That the Jews of Sosnowiec do not think much about spiritual matters is proved by the school "Vifre" [?]; but there are further proofs, and one of the most shameful is that a town of 25 thousand Jews has no Yiddish library (apart from the few books in the parties).
In Dąbrowa it is even worse. 5 thousand Jews live there, and the library at the Zionist org. is closed — no one needs a Yiddish book!
The activists of the Zionist org. buy Asch, Singer etc. in Polish translation, in order to bring the pennies into the library...
Zagłębie, i.e. the three main towns, counts some 65 thousand Jews, many thousands of young people, and all of them live their lives without a book, drawing their entire spiritual nourishment from newspapers.
And the outsider notices it more sharply and more painfully: all of Zagłębie has one idol, and it is called Katowice. By day one works hard [?], one "calls" [?] "shlagzakes" [?], one "tiyvirt" [?] (to the credit of the people of Zagłębie it must be said that they are truly industrious), and at night or on Sabbath and holidays one dreams (if one has no money) or one goes to Katowice.
And, to make the distinction: as once people debated a difficult Rambam, or the "[unclear word]" [?] — about Sokolow's [?] article, so now they discuss there the "Astoria", Café Club, "Waika", "Bagatela" and the like [cafés and venues in Katowice].
Katowice has become the Mecca of the Zagłębie youth. If one cannot afford to go into the "Waika", one strolls for a couple of hours along the little Third of May Street and goes home in peace [?]. Been in Katowice!
• • •
But we do not hold with moralising. We want to present the project, namely: in Zagłębie a central cultural organisation must be created, with its seat in Będzin (as the town in the middle), which is to unite all branches of cultural work. Within the society various sections will be organised: for literature, stage, music, local studies etc. All capable forces, regardless of their party affiliation, will join the society.
Every able young man will be attached to the section in which he can best express himself. The society is to be absolutely apolitical and to recognise the primacy of Yiddish, while including cultural work in Hebrew.
We sketch the project only in very general lines. We do not consider it the moment to go into details now. But we think that the cultural activists of Zagłębie ought to give the project some consideration and possibly open a discussion about it.
We, as outsiders, take the liberty of putting forward the idea. Let those who are interested in the question raised speak out.
It is certainly worth it!
Hadar HaCarmel – Mount Carmel.

[Palestine — Haifa; new road between Hadar HaCarmel and Mount Carmel; special report.]
Dov Rozman.
(Special for the "Zaglembier Tsaytung").

At a time when the Mufti and his gang are striving with all their might, by means of terror, to destroy the peaceful coexistence of the Arabs with the Jews, it is particularly worthwhile to dwell on the festive moment that Jewish and Arab Haifa experienced these days.

Nature has divided Haifa into 3 districts. The first — that is the city of Haifa with the port, where the population is mixed, with an Arab majority. The second — that is the Jewish Hadar HaCarmel, which lies about 30–60 metres above the city; and the third — is Mount Carmel, with its extraordinarily healthy climate, beautiful woods and gardens, wonderful villas and first-class hotels and boarding houses, and it lies about 160 metres above Hadar HaCarmel.

Until now only one road (about 8 km) connected the Hadar with the Mount, and almost the whole way one drives through [?] is — Arab.

In order, however, to have a direct connection between the Jewish Hadar HaCarmel and the Jewish Mount Carmel, the Hadar HaCarmel Committee (Va'ad) worked out, already several years ago, a plan to build a new road almost entirely across Jewish land, which belongs [?] — apart from a small number of private owners — mainly to Hachsharat HaYishuv and the KKL [Jewish National Fund], and which would at the same time shorten the way to about 5 km.

But here again came the usual intriguers, who saw in the plan a strengthening and an even greater consolidation of the Jewish position in Haifa, and [who] strove to have the plan not approved by the government.

Thanks to the untiring interventions of the Hadar HaCarmel Committee, with the help of the Haifa town council, where the mayor is the well-known liberal Mr. Hassan Shukri (on whom the Arab terrorists have already made 2 attempts on his life for not wanting to carry out their demands), it succeeded in convincing the government of the importance of the road, and a year ago. At the time when the terrorists awoke from their sleep, work began on realising the long-standing plan.

The wonderful, beautiful s-e-r-p-e-n-t-i-n-e road, supported in several places by concrete walls up to 10 metres high, is 3,100 metres long, from 10 to 15 metres wide, and is entirely covered with asphalt; it cost 17,000 pounds, in which the following took part: the Haifa municipality (magistrate) with 6,000 pounds, the Hadar HaCarmel Committee with 8,000 pounds, and the remaining 3,000 pounds were given by the private landowners.

The work was carried out by the "Misrad Kablani" [Solel Boneh contracting office], which employed 150 workers daily over the course of a year.

Although Palestine is known for its excellent road-building, the new road is regarded as the highest achievement to date.

The festive opening of the road took place in the presence of senior government officials, town council members, military representatives, representatives of all institutions and hundreds of invited guests.

The Arab mayor gave a warm speech about the importance of joint undertakings, which can only arise from joint work.

The chairman of the Hadar HaCarmel Committee, Mr. Elyanikov [?], stressed in his speech that today's celebration does not mean celebrating the victory of one people over the other, but on the contrary, the victory of the cooperation of 2 peoples, regardless of the fact that various factors are striving by all means to destroy the peaceful coexistence.

The Governor [District Commissioner], Mr. Keith-Roach, said among other things: "Coming here 6 years ago I found a desolate Haifa, and today Haifa already has 90 km of first-class paved streets and highways, and all this is owed solely to the joint cooperation of the Hadar HaCarmel Committee with the municipality"; and he expressed his warmest thanks to the untiring initiators and executors.

Then the Jewish deputy mayor, Mr. Shabtai Levy, handed the Governor Mr. Keith-Roach and the mayor Mr. Hassan [printed "Hazan"] Shukri the scissors to cut the 2 ribbons at one end and at the other, which was received with applause by the thousands present.

Then all the notables [?] and delegates went over to the well-known "Café Vienna" on Hadar HaCarmel, and at richly laid tables and in an elevated mood Mr. Elyanikov [?] presented the Governor Mr. Keith-Roach and the engineer Mr. Thomson with 2 albums about the works in Haifa by the Hadar HaCarmel Committee.

Haifa, April 1937.

The spiritual and material sides of the rabbinate question in Będzin
By Sh. Libaszon [?].

The rabbinate question in Będzin, which until now was wrapped in a "secret-filled" [?] veil, is taking on real forms. The "government military" has begun the attack and is trying to drive the "enemy" out of its hitherto "[—]" [?] positions.
Officially the battle began last Thursday afternoon, when the candidate of the "government camp" came to Będzin.
The first "reception" did not make on those attacked the proper impression that would have aroused any fear in them, and the one whom the "free elements" brought here — [—] be for the worse: who knows what, some little rebbe from a small shtetl with short sidelocks and... long [—], and above all — not from any rabbinic "core"; and after all is said and done — he speaks with a Lithuanian accent. People even say that he is an outstanding disciple of the Chofetz Chaim, of blessed memory, but that is still a small qualification for occupying the rabbinic seat of Będzin.
Those were the first "reports", which were soon spread through the town at the expense of the Mizrachi candidate.
The next day new winds suddenly began to blow, which aroused a melancholy mood in that camp; people grew frightened and began devising schemes of "wisdom [?] and wisdom"...
And at 2 o'clock in the afternoon special messengers were sent out with invitations to the members of the kehilla board, asking them to come — before the preparations for the Sabbath — to an extraordinary meeting taking place at 4 o'clock in the afternoon.
On the agenda of the meeting was a very important and urgent [item]. True, at this time Jews have plenty of urgent questions, but first of all the urgent question must be dealt with:
— "Should the Grajewo rabbi be allowed to preach in the synagogue on the Sabbath before the Torah reading?"
"The word went forth from before the king" — hardly had the invitations been sent out when the "general staff" of the "government front" [?] mobilised its forces, which were in the majority and indeed managed to repel the first attack...
Later the "[—]" was much easier, so that in the course of the Sabbath day almost "the whole town was taken" by the "government camp".
Only one "loss" is to be noted from the Sabbath "events", but the loss is a "small" one: for instance, while the rabbi was delivering a Torah discourse on Friday night, the fuses "protested" and blew...
About this "fuse blow-out", too, there are differences of opinion. Some say that a "miracle" really happened, since for many years no such blow-out had occurred, and some say that the power of the light of the rabbi's Torah prevailed over those who feel comfortable in the darkness (the rabbi-candidate calls them bats).
And the town was taken gradually [?], one position after another. On Friday, at the welcoming of the Sabbath, the town beit midrash was "taken", and the next day — the synagogue; but to "take" the synagogue it was necessary to use countless "bombs" — Torah bombs [?], which like a fountain sprayed forth genius, erudition, acumen, swam the sea of the Talmud in its length and breadth, kindled a fire in thousands of Jewish hearts, and a congregation stands enchanted and says:
— "A second Graubart", may he live long.
———
The next day, Sunday, something came out into the street and conveyed the impression of the Sabbath day. Jews stand around in "kupki" [little clusters], workaday Jews with workaday notions, and treat the rabbinate affair according to the real and "practical version".
— What use is all your cleverness to me — calls out a young Hasidic fellow, quite a "kol v'lakh" [?] in the A[lexande]r "shtibl" — you first have to convince me that a lion fights with a fly? But the Będzin rabbi will surely not be chosen according to rabbinic qualifications, only according to the sum one must "blacken" [? = bribe] several parnassim with.
— And here, on "that side", will money be lacking? — calls out a second — it may be that from "that side" there will be less money, but in my opinion the "takers" should surely take less, as long as good goods are delivered...
— The takers won't hear of it — calls out a third, a Jewish merchant — I happen to know that a certain parnas, an "old taker", is going about with a plan to create a "kulke" [? = kółko, ring] of the takers, so that the price will be uniform, according to the rate...
— Woe to the ears that hear this — an elderly householder joins in — I remember — he says — when a group of the most respected householders was delegated with a rabbinic letter of appointment to Rabbi Graubart, of blessed memory, and barely prevailed upon him to take over the rabbinic seat in Będzin, and today?...
The man wants to tell something more, but the conversation is interrupted by a flour broker, who turns to one of the participants in the conversation with the question whether he will buy a wagon of rye flour.
— A real stock exchange, upon my life: prices for parnassim's votes and prices for rye flour...
Oneg Shabbat (Sabbath Delight)

[Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings on the weekly portion.]
Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes around this week's portion
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Tazria-Metzora

a) "And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised" (12:3)
Reb Asherl of Stolin was once staying in a town of Misnagdim [opponents of Hasidism], and a Jew there honoured him with being sandek [godfather at a circumcision]. Reb Asherl kept everyone waiting for him a long time. When he arrived late at the bris, one of the relatives of the father of the child, a Jew who was a dyed-in-the-wool Misnaged, came up to him and said insolently:
— You let Elijah the Prophet wait for you so long?
Reb Asherl looked at him and answered with a smile:
— No harm done, Elijah can wait..
That made the Misnaged boil even more, and he angrily asked Reb Asherl:
— What? Perhaps you were studying all this time?
Reb Asherl smiles again:
— I was not studying, I was simply eating. But Elijah is an angel and does not need to eat, needs no money, so he can wait for a wretched creature of flesh and blood who needs money, must eat and so on..

b) "The plague of leprosy" (13:2[?])
The end of Parashat Shemini is devoted to forbidden foods, and the beginning of Parashat Tazria-Metzora is devoted straight away to the laws of the leper. What is the connection behind this juxtaposition?
First the Torah speaks about not eating unclean animals and the like — in that, people are still more or less careful. Then come the laws[?] of leprosy, which comes because of slander [lashon hara], that is, eating living people... The Torah means to show that eating a living person is graver even than forbidden foods...
Reb Israel Salanter.
* * *
"None is richer than the pig and none poorer than the dog" — [—]
When a Jew eats pork he is a transgressor of Israel. Pork is the "most proper" prohibition, that is, everyone does respect this prohibition. About slander it is said "Whoever speaks lashon hara deserves to be thrown to the dogs" (Pesachim 118), and in that people are so little careful — "none poorer than the dog": it is the poorest prohibition...
Or la-Olam.
* * *
"If I say, I will speak thus [kemo], behold, I should betray the generation of Thy children" [Ps. 73:15].
There are prohibitions which are in the category of "as if" [kemo], because they are not stated explicitly in the Torah — for example slander; it is only said "Whoever speaks lashon hara is as if he worshipped idols". So it is an "as-if" prohibition, and in these "as-if sins" people are so little careful. "If I say, I will speak kemo" — if I were to enumerate these as-if sins, "behold, I should betray the generation of Thy children" — it would turn out that even "Thy children", the righteous, are traitors...
Reb Zvi Hirsh Harazitsh[?].
* * *
In the Shemoneh Esreh prayer we say:
"My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit... and let my soul be as dust to all; open my heart to Thy Torah."
What sense does this juxtaposition have?
The Gemara gives us: "What is the remedy for one who speaks lashon hara? If he is a scholar, let him engage in Torah; and if he is an ignoramus, let him humble himself." So the remedies against slander are engaging in Torah and keeping oneself low. Therefore we say: to be guarded from slander — "let my soul be as dust to all, open my heart to Thy Torah": one must hold oneself like the earth and engage in Torah..
Nahalat Uziel.

c) "And he shall be brought to the priest" (derash).
In Parashat Korach, on the verse "as the Lord said to him by the hand of Moses", Rashi says: "Whoever disputes the priesthood is struck with leprosy". That is why the leper's punishment is to be brought to the priest...
Kol Yevaser.

d) "It is all turned white: he is clean" (derash, 13[?]).
"Rabbi Isaac said: The son of David will not come until the whole kingdom is turned to heresy, as it is said: It is all turned white — he is clean." Sanhedrin 93 [as printed; the source is Sanhedrin 97].
"Until the whole kingdom is turned to heresy" means: racism. Every nation will regard itself as a chosen race, as "white", as the purest and most chosen race... And in truth this bloodthirsty[?] "white"[?] racism is the true sign of[?] the Messiah..
Rabbi Samson Raphael Hirsch.

e) "This shall be the law of the leper" (14:2[?])
Leprosy comes for the sin of slander. And unfortunately the sin of slander is often found precisely among the men of Torah, and that is what the expression "Torat ha-metzora" [the law/Torah of the leper] means...
Zer Zahav.
* * *
"The two of them are written in the book of remembrance" (Berakhot 8)
If two scholars sit and study, their words are written in the book of remembrance. For when two scholars sit together, engage in Torah and speak no slander about a third scholar, then truly[?] they ought to be inscribed in the book of remembrance...
Imrei Emet.

f) "And he shall dwell outside his tent" (derash, 8)
The Sages say that a leper must stay outside the camp because he was haughty and kept himself apart from people; therefore, as a leper, he must sit apart from people. One asks: but why must he sit "outside his tent", apart from his own household?
Because —
"He who is haughty is not accepted even by his own household" — the household suffers most of all from a haughty man; therefore he must keep apart from them too..
Reb Shmelke of Nikolsburg [Mikulov].
Interesting things we know nothing about.

Everyone and his brother talks today of only one thing: England. Not only about how the coronation will be held, but also about England itself — what it looks like there, how life is lived in England, and so on.
It is therefore worth describing a few interesting things, some of which the writer experienced himself on his travels in England and some of which the writer heard from distinguished Englishmen.
Once we were again at a press meeting of the Leipzig Fair, and the main word was held, as always, by John[?] Stoops, the editor of the London "Times". Of course England was discussed, and Stoops asked whether anyone among us knew how many inhabitants London has. Of course there were several who knew exactly, according to the latest census: 7 million 476 thousand 886 inhabitants.
Mister Stoops smiled the little smile that all editors of the "Times" have, who know better.
You are mistaken; London has altogether 9834 inhabitants. Don't laugh, I don't mean some little town somewhere in the world that is also called London. I mean precisely the capital of the British Empire: London. This city counts altogether 9834 inhabitants, and this year it recorded 83 newborns and 51 deaths.
You must know that the real London is only the inner city, "the City"; the rest was added to London over the course of many years. But "the City" has indeed remained the actual city, with special laws and with its own mayor, the "Lord Mayor". The whole rest of the city is administered by councillors. Only the 9834 inhabitants of the "City" have a mayor, the only one in London. All laws come into force in the "City" only once the Lord Mayor has confirmed them. The "City" has its own member in Parliament, although it has so few voters; it has its own police, and the police of the other English towns, even of the other parts of London, may not do any service there; they may not interfere in the affairs of the "City burghers".
True, all day long there are in the "City", where the big businesses and offices are open, about two million people and more, who buy and sell. But when the businesses and offices close, everyone leaves "London City" and only 9834 people remain there, who live there permanently.
The great Holborn Street is on its right side "London", and on its left side it belongs to the "suburb". At ten o'clock at night one can see thousands of people coming out of the establishments on the right side of Holborn Street and crossing over to the restaurants and establishments on the same street on the left, because in "London" all establishments and restaurants must close at ten o'clock, while outside London one may keep them open as long as the police permit.
The same can be seen on Sunday. On the right side of Holborn Street all restaurants and tea-houses are closed because of the Sunday rest, and on the left side of the same street all establishments are open — there is music, dancing and merriment...
In "London" there is a hostel which was opened in the year 1579 by the millionaire of that time, Watts[?]. This hostel has only twelve beds. According to the will of Watts[?], which is today guarded by a special company of rich men, the guests of the house receive not only a fine, clean lodging and the best food free of charge, but everyone who leaves receives in addition a shilling as provision for the road... In this hostel all guests who have stayed there during the 358 years are registered. The most distinguished people in the world are recorded there, among them also the English Queen Elizabeth. Every day the "hotel" is occupied by the finest and best guests who come to "London".
Z. Haber, Vienna.
A day of gratitude...

[Będzin — personalities; jubilee; public life.] (From the 40th-anniversary jubilee in honour of Dr. S. Weinzieher [Dr. Salomon Weinzieher, physician, former Sejm deputy] in Będzin.)
Jewish public life in Zagłębie, and Będzin in particular, celebrated last Sabbath the festival of the 40 years of cultural and public activity of Dr. S. Weinzieher.
The celebration turned out very imposing; it was truly a Jewish demonstration for a person who embodies in himself the essence of a communal worker, one who occupies himself faithfully with the needs of the public. The cream of the Jewish intelligentsia of Zagłębie gathered, and a large number — from Sosnowiec. The mood — festive, the surroundings — warm; the splendidly lit hall of the "Orphans' Home", the richly laid tables, the living flowers caused one to forget a little the day-to-day calamities [?] befalling the Jewish people.
In the street where the "Orphans' Home" is located there is a stir of cars and droshkies bringing the guests. The entrance to the assembly hall is decorated with garlands and flower pots. The number of guests grows from minute to minute and reaches nearly 300; people greet and kiss one another like close in-laws at a wedding, and through the hall goes [?] the word: "They are coming!..."
All eyes turn to the main entrance, where the close family of the jubilarian arrives, among them also Dr. Wein[zi]eher [?] of Warsaw, a friend [?], who came specially for the celebration, and right after them — Dr. Weinzieher, his wife and their children. The hall trembles with the warm ovation given in honour of the jubilarian; the moment is a moving one, the whole audience rises from their seats, and a large number of children, who were up in the gallery, sing "Sto lat" with piano accompaniment by Miss Ella [?] Landner.
After the jubilarian with his family, and also the jubilee committee, have taken the seats reserved for them, the celebration is opened with a short speech by Mrs. Cesia [?] Szajn, and president S. Fürstenberg [Szymon Fürstenberg] is invited as toastmaster [?]; he delivers a very warm greeting in the name of the Jewish public of Będzin and also in his own name.
In his greeting Mr. Fürstenberg underlines the merits of the jubilarian as a communal worker, as a "citizen", as a loyal son of the Jewish people and especially as a resident of Będzin, and he wishes him to live and be active until a hundred and twenty years.
Mrs. Ts. Szajn gives a survey of Dr. Weinzieher's activity from the moment he settled in Będzin until the present day.
Mr. A. Liher — [on behalf of?] the Zionist org.; in the name of the former he appraised the abilities of the jubilarian and singled him out as the Jewish representative of Zagłębie Jewry; he wishes him to live to see the festival of the Jewish redemption.
Dr. Ferber says that Dr. Weinzieher is the one who holds high the ethics of his profession.
Dr. Herzman (Sosnowiec) — Dr. Weinzieher is always our guide; we are his pupils, who listen with great respect to his opinions.
A fine greeting is given by Dr. T. Liberman (Sosnowiec), who appraises the merits of Dr. Weinzieher as director of the Jewish hospital in Sosnowiec, which is also a "home" for the young doctors, also as a public worker for the community and especially as president of the Orphans' Home; in the name of the medical staff he wishes him further success in his work.
In the name of the Zionist Organisation, president Mr. Wygodzki speaks; he expresses the view that the town of Będzin is [too] small to be able to appreciate the public merits of Dr. Weinzieher.
Then greetings were given: in the name of "WIZO" — its president Mrs. Wager [?]; from the Doctors' Association — Dr. Rapaport; from the "Ognisko" — Mr. Żmudzki; and from the board of "Dobroczynność" [?] — Mr. Stawin [?] Masak; in the name of the Jewish artisan masses — Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn.
Also speaking about Dr. Weinzieher are Adv. Kohn (Sosnowiec), Herman Szer, N. Landner, M. Lewin and others.
Dozens of telegrams are also read out, among others from Katowice, Sosnowiec, Będzin, Częstochowa, Warsaw, Łódź, and also from the Directorate of the Keren Kayemet (JNF) in Jerusalem, which announces that the jubilee committee has inscribed Dr. Weinzieher in the Golden Book.
Of the Jewish communities (kehillot) in Zagłębie, only the Jewish community in Zawiercie sent a greeting.
A very successful attraction was the appearance of Mrs. Distefeld [?] (Katowice), who sang very beautifully a series of arias and also the folk songs "Eli Eli" and "Kh'vil nisht zayn keyn rebbe" ["I don't want to be a rebbe"], for which the singer was rewarded with strong applause. Miss Landner too performed several compositions very well.
The closing word goes to the honoured jubilarian Dr. Weinzieher, who speaks in his own manner, a little serious, a little humorous. "I wonder," he says, "why I have been paid so many compliments, had so many praises enumerated — what for? After all, I am no rich man from whom one expects to obtain a good post and the like. If," he says, "I have given away so many years for the good of society, it is only because I was born with such a character; already from my earliest youth I was nagged by the question why individuals should have so much good while the community suffers?"
At the end of the speech the doctor is very moved, especially when he says that a great share in this festival belongs to his life's companion, who never hindered him in his public work (both kiss, and the whole audience sings "Sto lat" in honour of the doctor's wife).
The closing speech is given by president Mr. Fürstenberg, who once more expresses a wish to the jubilarian, as well as thanks to the participants, and stresses that the celebration will remain a lasting memory for everyone.
After a series of photographs has been taken by the owner of "Studio", the celebration is closed at 3 o'clock at dawn.
S. L—sz.
A. Zaglembier — The Living Dead Man (4)

[Literature — serialised novel.] A. Zaglembier: The Living Dead Man. (A highly suspenseful novel of Jewish life in Zagłębie before and after the World War). 4)
Summary of the beginning of the novel.
On a winter evening before the World War, when two Cossacks were to transfer the dangerous bandit „Szmulek Łapka“ to the Piotrków prison, they were suddenly attacked on the way to the station by two disguised „strażniks“ [guards] — Łapka's helpers. The Cossacks were found at dawn[?] lying bound, with gagged mouths, and Szmulek „Łapka“, freed, escaped to the Gzichów[?] road and is hiding somewhere.
The same evening, and almost at the same hour, the widely („everywhere“) known, respectable debt-collector [inkasent] Josl Wertheim — a father of three children — suddenly disappeared. His wife Sorele[?] runs about the town terribly desperate, searching[?] for him in all the police [—] of the whole of Zagłębie. But Josl Wertheim has vanished like a stone in water...
Everyone already considers[?] it an extraordinary[?] riddle. Finally, on the seventh day, the pock-marked Wacek reports to police inspector Charecki and gives explanations about the vanished Wertheim.
Now read on.
Charecki pretended not to notice Wacek's embarrassment and went on:
— So you saw Wertheim on Wednesday; you remember it exactly?
— Quite exactly.
— Do you perhaps also remember when it was, by day or by night?
— Oh, in the evening.
— How late could it have been then, roughly?
— Ah, the sun had already set, somewhere between 8 and 9 in the evening.
Charecki kept taking notes and asked:
— You remember exactly, between 8 and 9.
— Yes.
— And where was it? I mean in what place, in what street?
— It was on the Gzichów[?] road, further up.
— What were you doing there then?
— I was walking from Grojce [Grodziec?], I had been at my uncle's.
— And in which direction was Josl Wertheim going? Into town?
— No, further up towards the woods, towards Gzichów[?].
— And was Josl Wertheim going alone?
— No, with somebody else...
Charecki again gave a nervous start from his seat, and his tension rose to the highest degree. At last, — he thought with satisfaction, — it is beginning to get a little lighter in this dark affair...
— And who was the other one, with whom Josl Wertheim was walking? A man, a woman?
— A pani [a Polish lady]... — Wacek answered quietly.
— What? A pani? A Jewish woman? Would you recognise her?
— I know her very well, but she is not Jewish...
— Who is she?
— Wanda Komarska, the miller's daughter, the beautiful one.
— You saw both of them that evening on the Gzichów road?
— Yes.
— And did they see you too?
— No. Because when I came from the Grojce road, they had already passed a bit further on. But I recognised them well, because they had walked that road together several times already...
From minute to minute the police inspector was more and more astonished, hearing Wacek's clear answer, for it was still easy to see that the pock-marked man was telling the truth.
— And when did you see them walking along the same road before that time too?
— Three weeks ago.
— And also in the evening?
— Yes.
— And were you then also coming back from Grojce?
— Not that time...
Why then were you interested in where the two of them were going?...
To this question too[?] the pock-marked Wacek found no answer...
But for that very reason Wacek's sudden silence told Charecki more than speech... and at once an idea occurred to him, through which the mysterious riddle became even clearer to the police inspector... And after contemplating Wacek for a longer while, he suddenly asked him:
— Are you married already?
— No.
— And do you have a fiancée?...
— I had...
— Who is she?...
— The same one... Wanda Komarska... But since she started going about with the Jewish debt-collector, with that Josek Wertheim, she has thrown me over...
Once again the police inspector jerked from his seat on hearing Wacek's last words. And looking still more sharply into the pock-marked man's eyes, Charecki raised his voice somewhat.
— Now I understand... Josl Wertheim was your rival in love... and that is why you spied on them on their secret walks?... Yes?..
It seems[?] that police inspector Charecki had hit upon the truth, for after his last words Wacek's pock-marked face turned even redder. He was especially ashamed of the word „spied“, which Charecki had said to him:
— Well, was it really so? — Charecki now asks in a milder tone, seeing that Wacek had again become as if stunned — why don't you answer? After all, we did not send for you, nobody suspects you of anything bad either... You came to us yourself... I must ask you all this, because a human life is at stake here! The tragic occurrence in our town must be uncovered, and if you help us with it you will certainly be rewarded... Well then?
These words did indeed give Wacek courage, and he became bolder.
— Yes — he answers — that Josek Wertheim really is my rival, but I have nothing against him. I know that it was not he who ran after her, but she after him, such a carrion [ścierwo]... And that is why she broke off with me and stopped being my fiancée.
— But why did you use to follow them on their walks?
— — I love her — Wacek lowers his eyes — they would not let me into her house, Wanda would not allow it... so I wanted to wait for her when she would come back from the „randka“ [date] with her Jewish lover.
— Oh, is that so — Charecki again throws him a suspicious glance — very interesting[?]... So that evening too you waited until she would come back from the „randka“ with Josek Wertheim?
— Yes.
— And did you wait until she came?
— Yes, it took more than an hour until she came back.
— Who?
— Wanda.
— Wait... wait... — a hopeful gleam appeared in Charecki's eyes and he feverishly began to draw with his pencil — so it was Wanda alone who came back from the walk?
— Yes, she alone.
— And Wertheim? You did not see him come back?
— No.
— Very interesting[?]... Did[?] the fact strike you that Wanda came back all alone?
— No, not then, only a few days later, when I heard that Wertheim had vanished without a trace that evening..
— Yes, I understand — Charecki is pleased that[?] at last the mystery is being cleared up for him — well, and what did Wanda say to you then?
— Nothing. She did not want to speak to me at all, she even swore at me and ran off.
(To be continued).
The Cooking Ladle. The "President". (A Little Portrait).

I know a Jew, a "chinen"[?]:
he stammers a little —
(no matter what he's called there[?]:
Pesach, Moshe, Nisl..)

This Jew, gentlemen,
is no great scholar —
nor can one put any wisdom
into him, into his "gdn"[?]...

He is a simple little Jew,
a plain living soul,
no Hasid, no Torah scholar
and no God-fearing man either.

But with this little Jew
there is a very great trouble:
he suffers from a kind of mania
called — "presidentitis"...

And it is a grave weakness[?],
a disease and an ailment —
everywhere he pushes himself in
and grabs the "president's chair"...

And this little Jew already holds
a great many presidencies —
he has suffered from this complaint
for a long time, almost years..

And[?] the "President" has a habit:
he wants to measure up to [important] people —
so he pours out "congress" words —
till you hold your sides [laughing]...

One may call him, without exaggeration,
"the president over all presidents";
the title "esteemed president"
is dearer to him than food..

And after a hundred and twenty years
they will inscribe on his tombstone:
"Here lies the well-known president,
to you[?] every male and every female..."

— — — — —

I know a Jew, a "chinen"[?],
he stammers a little —
(no matter what he's called there[?] —
Pesach, Moshe, Nisl...)
He suffers from a disease,
he suffers from a trouble —
its name is very simple:
pre—si—den—titis.
Sh-M.
A Toast Not Given.

The "Kokh-Lefl" [Cooking Ladle] wanted to give a toast last Saturday night at the orphanage, but since he was afraid that all those speeches might bring on a flood... he gave up, and now he takes the "floor".
My ladies (I don't literally mean "mine"... That's a good one! That's all I'd need for my hard "pleasant"[?] lot — to have such a harem of wives, God forbid, God preserve us...), so then, ladies and gentlemen, misses and cavaliers, or homely comrade, common-folk craftsman, and the whole Zionist family — "C.K." Zionists and "Schwarzbardists"[?] and all kinds of "-ists", who for a moment forgot their differentiations-nuances and their party interests and came together here at one table, like a "sorbet"[?], all together, with one drink, with one feeling. It is truly a great "miracle" that such an idyll can happen among Jews only through "eating"... Well then, be greeted — and blessed [pun: "bagrist" — "banist"]..
Now I raise the glass and call out:
L'chaim! Long may our dear Dr. R' Shlomo live, because we have no one else fit to take his place. I wish him truly countless blessings, and above all that he may yet be privileged to be called "naczelny lekarz" [chief physician] in our "ojczyzna" [fatherland], in the Land of Israel.
Amotsl[?].
Night-Watchmen of All Courtyards, Unite!

From the Zagłębie Night-Watchmen's Association the "Kokh-Lefl" [Cooking Ladle] has received an appeal, which we reproduce almost word for word:
To all sleepless comrades:
At last the time has come against those who loll[?] on their soft "sheniks"[?] all night. While the drowsy bourgeois dream of an interest-free loan, we cannot even do any "dushim"[?].
Who knows better than we what goes on at night? The merchants make their "balances" at night; the textile manufacturers "search for chametz" in their warehouses at night; the money from the flower-days is counted at night; if a man wants to "petemoviyen"[?] with his wife, he does it at night; if a "słomiany wdowiec" [straw widower] wants to smuggle "something" through and fears the evil eye, he does it at night — everything at night!
Our demands are:
1) Sweep the courtyards only by day[?]; at night let the bourgeois keep watch [pilnować] themselves.
2) Every night-watchman must be given a mattress with a pillow, and for being woken — a special gratification.
3) For married night-watchmen: they must be warned when "zastępcy" [substitutes] are about, who are to "entertain"[?] the wives so that they do not "grieve"[?] in the time of husbandlessness.
Long live the organized sleepless proletariat!
Down with the magnates who loll[?] on soft "sheniks"[?]!
We close with the call: Comrades, do not sleep — wake up[?]!
The Night-Watchmen's Association
in Zagłębie.

What Is Heard in Zagłębie? / Będzin / They Didn't Hit the Right Address...

[Będzin — Swindle; Kehilla; Zionism.]
[Page head: Friday 5 Iyar 5697 — Friday 16 April 1937]
What is heard in Zagłębie?
Będzin
They didn't hit the right address...
On Tuesday at midday Mr. Berl Granat[?] was walking along Małachowskiego Street when an unknown man came up to him and asked Granat in Russian where a police commissariat was.
"Right here, not far, at Małachowskiego 16 there is a commissariat," Granat answered, and went off.
After a few steps G. is stopped by a young Jewish man who asks: "What did the 'katsap' [derogatory for a Russian] ask you?"
"He asked me where a commissariat is," Granat explained.
"Do me a favour, uncle[?]," the young man begins to plead, "and prevail on the 'katsap' to sell you the diamond earrings. He stood in our jewellery shop on Małachowskiego 7 and I already wanted to give him 1200 zł., and he doesn't want to; so [...][?] go, Mr. Jew, and negotiate with him, because it's a pity to me that such a 'bargain' should fall to someone else."
Granat let himself be persuaded, went after the 'katsap' and asked him why he does not want to sell the earrings to the Jew.
"He has 'Żydowskie' [Jewish] money, and also [...] he[?] will give me forged banknotes; to this one[?] I'll sell."
The young man began to tell[?] stories until he managed to bring the 'seller' together with the 'buyer'; all of them went into the gateway of Frachcwajg's[?] house on Piłsudskiego Street, where the 'transaction' was to take place. Granat[?], who had by then figured out the 'deal', turned[?] to the young man with the complaint:
"Why don't you buy the diamonds? After all I've already done everything for your sake!"
"Wait here downstairs and I'll run for father, who will bring money."
When the young man went off after the 'father', the 'Russian' meanwhile proposed to Granat that he buy the 'bargain', and if he did not have all the money on him, he should meanwhile give a 'zadatek' [deposit][?]; he would even hand over the 'diamonds' beforehand.
It did not take long before the 'father' came, who, on seeing Granat, gave a sign that the 'deal' would not be made, and all three went off to look for fresh 'customers'...

A Year After the Wedding the "Secret" Is Discovered

[Będzin — Family and Rabbinate.]
On Podzamcze Street lived a young woman with a small child. To the "street" it was said that the woman was a divorcee; only a few knew that her husband had run away from her and left her a living agunah.
The young wife found favour with a young man from the same street, and soon the couple married.
The couple lived quite contentedly, until a black cat ran between them. The "black cat" is her first husband, who, learning that his wife had married, came here and told the second husband the whole truth. At first the woman tried to deny it, but when the husband gave her all the "signs", she finally admitted that because she had wanted to marry, she had passed herself off as a divorcee.
The epilogue of this story was played out this week before the local rabbinate, which ruled that the woman must receive a get from both husbands.
The first husband, who had only sought to take revenge on his wife, vanished immediately[?] after revealing the "secret". The second husband too no longer wanted to go on like this[?] and gave her a get.
Sosnowiec — Verdict in the Trial of 9 Bomb-Throwers

[Sosnowiec — crime, antisemitism.]
The trial of 9 bomb-throwers, who were accused of carrying out a series of bomb attacks, took place at the local District Court. One attack was, as is known, carried out on the beit midrash in Pogoń, and the explosion killed 13-year-old Moshe Rozenblum. Besides this, an attack was carried out on the Jewish Gelibter family, and 5 persons were wounded. Another bomb attack was carried out on the Hotel “Bristol”.
The accused were defended by 8 lawyers. 35 witnesses were summoned to the trial, among them 11 Jewish victims.
The accused did not admit to the [—] [illegible word; probably: the deeds], but [claimed] that the explosive materials found on them had been prepared not against Jews but against Communists.
After the speeches of the defence the verdict was pronounced, under which the chief defendant, the chairman of the Endek party Heinzinger, was sentenced to a year and a half in prison, Grudniewicz to 10 months, Wiadocki[?] to 8 months; the others were acquitted.

Merin — in charge of the premises, Mr. Lederman — board[?] member, and Mr. Grinbojm as head of the most active sections of the society.
It should be mentioned on this occasion that the “Lira” society, with the [?] academy (perhaps a Purim academy) that it organised not long ago, proved to the Sosnowiec public that it is beginning to reach a proper cultural level, devoting such fine events to the broad Jewish population.
As we learn, the newly elected board has already set about active work, and soon a series of dramatic-musical undertakings will be organised, in which the choir, the drama section and the music section will take a lively part.

Altman, who greeted all the guests present and invited to the presidium the local moreh hora'ah Szwarc, the shochet David Cwajgenhaft, and Messrs. Lichtensztajn, S. Altman, Jurkiewicz, Woszyca[?], Fiszel, Abramowicz and Glidman.
After honouring the fallen in Eretz Israel, as well as the deceased board members Lichtensztajn, Szmulewicz and Libner, the floor was taken by the vice-chairman Mr. Fajerman, who outlined in brief strokes the useful work and the past of the Gemilut Hesed fund. Another Hasidic Lad “Kidnapped”

[Sosnowiec — Hasidism, family.]
A few months ago the Edlich brothers were “kidnapped” to Ger [Góra Kalwaria]. After much effort the family succeeded in getting the “kidnapped” back.

Feverish work in the Sandomierz region

[Kielce and region — economy and employment.] Over 3,000 workers are employed in the work.

Because of the enormous works, hundreds of people from the "sumrisher"[?] (doubtful reading) arrive daily in the Sandomierz region in search of work[?].
The first works are being carried out in electrifying the local area, as well as in laying the foundations of a number of factories.
The life of the home-working shoe-upper stitchers.

[Kielce — artisans.] The annual general meeting of the Kielce "shtepper-chałupnicy" (home-working stitchers of shoe uppers), which took place a few days ago, showed that the board of the Kielce home-working stitchers has led the life of the Kielce master stitchers onto straight paths.
Over 20 members were present at the general meeting; the meeting was opened by the starszy (head of the guild) Grynsztajn. Mr. Nysmanowicz[?] was elected chairman.
The activity report was delivered by starszy Grynsztajn. From the report one heard that lately the work of the guild had been hampered, and the board could not carry on normal activity because of the audit, during which the books and other documents of the guild were taken away.
Nevertheless the board stood at its post and did not neglect the interests of the members. The last pre-holiday campaign also passed off peacefully, giving the merchants the possibility of not interrupting the work.
Starszy Grynsztajn discusses the financial situation of the guild and shows that the guild has worked without a deficit.
A budget for the year 1937 was drawn up, which was adopted by those assembled.
Elected as starszy was Mr. G. Grynsztajn, as podstarszy (deputy head) Mr. D. Pomerancblum; elected to the board were Messrs.: Sz. Drewniany[?], H. Herling[?], D. Wiślicki, Sz. Wajsbrot, J. Moszkowicz, H. Kac.

Dr. Tad. Zaderecki's Lecture in Katowice

[Katowice — lecture.] (L. S.) In the large "Powstańców"[?] hall in Katowice, on Sunday evening, the well-known Polish Talmud expert Dr. Zaderecki lectured[?] on the Jewish cultural treasures contained in the Tanakh and the Talmud — religious, universal and national.
The speaker explains, briefly[?], about the Giving of the Torah, why the Jews and no other peoples took the Torah, and how highly Jews esteem the learned man, the man of scholarship.
It is only a pity that our neighbours did not hear how the pure Aryan Zaderecki unmasks the "Talmud experts", the Trzeciaks and others, by quoting their "works".
The lecturer criticised our intelligentsia: only the various [—] remind them of their heritage and traditions; they do not trouble themselves to learn and know Jewish scholarship, nor do they use the possibilities, through translations, of enabling the Poles, with whom we have lived together so long, to study us.
This idealistic friend of ours truly needs a great deal of courage in present times to give such lectures. He is truly self-sacrificing, and therefore the large number of listeners applauded him warmly.
The mohel “didn't give a hoot”...

[Upper Silesia — community.] We are written from Nowa Wieś[?]:
Last week an outrage crying to heaven took place here, committed by the mohel Z. of Sosnowiec.
At the home of a local Jewish broker[?] a circumcision (bris) was to take place. He travelled to Sosnowiec, where he engaged the mohel Z.
At the appointed time the mohel came to Nowa Wieś and preparations for the bris began. As few Jewish inhabitants live in the place, the father of the child went out to the market, from where he “grabbed” several Jews from Zagłębie to make up the minyan.
All preparations were complete, the candles on the table were burning, the godfather (kvater) handed the child to the sandek, and —
— “Woe is me!” — cries the father.
— What happened? — asks the crowd curiously.
— The mohel is gone.
People run[?] to search in every corner of the town, but “and the lad is not there” [printed: “ותגער איננו”], the mohel is gone..
Having no choice, the candles were put out and the crowd dispersed.
The new mother, hearing what had happened, simply went into spasms[?], and with great difficulty she was calmed.
Later it turned out that the same mohel had been engaged for a bris in Sosnowiec at 12 noon, and an hour later in Chorzów[?], and knowing that because of the bris in Nowa Wieś he would be late for the circumcisions in Sosnowiec and Chorzów[?] — he “fled” (vayivrach).
He came back to Nowa Wieś only at 5 in the afternoon, and only then did the bris take place.

Nearly two and a half million savings books.

[Economy — Postal Savings Bank.] (Yta) Every month more than 50 thousand new depositors in savings books, and on average 8—10 million złoty in new savings deposits — this is certainly on the one hand good[?] proof of habitual[?] saving among the broad strata of the population and of wise capitalisation, and on the other hand an evident sign of the unshaken trust that the population has in the P.K.O. [Pocztowa Kasa Oszczędności, Postal Savings Bank].
The figures given above on the average growth of the savings service of the P.K.O. for the first quarter of this year: the sum of savings deposits in the P.K.O. grew in that quarter by more than 25 million zł., and by 1 April reached a total of 689 million zł.
But still more characteristic is the steady growth of new depositors of savings books, which this year reached record figures, namely: January 53.445, February 56,907, March 51,791, so that on 1 April the total number[?] of savings books in the PKO reached 2.416.849.
Nearly two and a half million savings books — these are, expressed in the language of figures, those great advantages which the PKO assures its clients, among other things[?], in the field of saving. This is the expression of the full trust of savers in the proven security of PKO deposits.
